answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to earn a reputation bond before it can transact — an opal formed under pressure, not handed out at signup. New identities start near zero trust and gain weight only through verified, useful work over time, the way a glacier moves: slow, visible, and impossible to fake overnight. A light zephyr of free entry stays open for genuine newcomers, but any identity that tries to clone itself must repeat the same cold, patient climb from zero, so mass fakery costs more than it can ever earn.
